prompt: You add 0.3 equivalents of CH₃MgBr to a solution containing BOTH 2-butanone (a ketone) and methyl benzoate (an ester). Which carbonyl absorbs most of the Grignard?

options.label: The ketone — it's more electrophilic than the ester, so the limited Grignard reacts with it preferentially.
Both equally — the carbonyl carbons have similar electrophilicity, so statistical distribution.
The ester — the π-donating OR group makes the ester carbon more polarized and more reactive.
Neither — at 0.3 eq the Grignard is quenched by trace moisture before any addition occurs.

explanation: Esters have resonance donation from the -OR oxygen that spreads the C=O π density and LOWERS electrophilicity at carbon. Ketones have no such donor → more electrophilic. With sub-stoichiometric Grignard, chemoselectivity emerges: ketone wins.
